response.sql: WITH order_rates AS (SELECT u.acctscope, o.recordvault, AVG(f.feerate) - AVG(f.rebrate) AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope, o.recordvault), scope_stats AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM order_rates WHERE net_rate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, order_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_of_scope_avgs FROM scope_stats

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault uniquely identifies an order and users.userstamp uniquely identifies a user, so the joins do not duplicate fee rows.
An order's net rate is missing when either its average feerate or its average rebrate is NULL (all values NULL). Such orders are excluded from the scope average and from the order count.
The comparison value is the unweighted mean of the per-scope average net rates. Scopes with no qualifying orders do not appear in the output and are not part of that mean.
